   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>NOTE</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Organization</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Independence Realty Trust, Inc. (&#8220;IRT&#8221;), is a self-administered and self-managed Maryland corporation that was formed on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 26, 2009 </em>and that has elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust (&#8220;REIT&#8221;). We are primarily engaged in the ownership, operation, management, improvement, and acquisition of multifamily apartment communities in non-gateway markets. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we owned and operated&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725799" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:NumberOfPropertiesMultifamilyApartments" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">115</ix:nonFraction>&#160;multifamily apartment properties (including <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725800">one</span> owned through a consolidated joint venture) that contain an aggregate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725801" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfUnitsInRealEstateProperty" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">33,602</ix:nonFraction> units across non-gateway U.S. markets, including Atlanta, Columbus, Dallas, Denver, Houston, Indianapolis, Nashville, Oklahoma City, Raleigh-Durham, and Tampa. In addition, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we owned <span style="color: #000000; "><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725802">two</span> newly developed properties that are currently in lease-up, including <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725803">one</span></span>&#160;in Denver, Colorado, that&#160;contains&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725804" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-DenverColoradoMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:NumberOfUnitsInRealEstatePropertiesUponCompletion" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">296</ix:nonFraction>&#160;units and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725805">one</span>&#160;in Austin, Texas, that&#160;contains <ix:nonFraction id="c143725806" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_StatementGeographicalAxis-AustinTexasMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:NumberOfUnitsInRealEstatePropertiesUponCompletion" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">378</ix:nonFraction> units. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we also owned interest<span style="color:#000000;">s in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725807">three</span>&#160;unco</span>nsolidated joint ventures, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725808">one</span>&#160;of which owns and operates a multifamily apartment community&#160;that contains&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725809" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:NumberOfUnitsInRealEstatePropertyMultifamilyApartmentCommunities" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">275</ix:nonFraction><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span>units and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725810">two</span>&#160;of which&#160;are&#160;developing&#160;multifamily apartment communities&#160;that will, upon completion, contain an aggregate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725811" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:NumberOfUnitsInRealEstatePropertyMultifamilyApartmentProperties" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">642</ix:nonFraction>&#160;units. We own all of our assets and conduct substantially all of our operations through Independence Realty Operating Partnership, LP, a Delaware limited partnership (&#8220;IROP&#8221;), of which we are the sole general partner.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As used herein, the terms &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; refer to IRT and, as required by context, IROP and its subsidiaries.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3166649" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727879" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>a. Basis of Presentation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The accompanying unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared by management in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). Certain information and footnote disclosures normally included in annual consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP have been condensed or omitted pursuant to such rules and regulations, although we believe that the included disclosures are adequate to make the information presented <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> misleading. The unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with our audited financial statements as of and for the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> included in our&#160;Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 (</em>the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2025</em> Annual Report&#8221;). In the opinion of management, all adjustments, consisting only of normal recurring adjustments, necessary to present fairly our condensed consolidated financial position and condensed consolidated results of operations and cash flows are included. The results of operations for the interim periods presented are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the results for the full year. The Company evaluated subsequent events through the date its financial statements were issued. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> significant recognized or non-recognized subsequent events were noted other than those described in the footnotes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727880" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>b. Principles of Consolidation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The condensed consolidated financial statements reflect our accounts and the accounts of IROP and its subsidiaries. All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. Pursuant to the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification Topic <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> &#8220;Consolidation&#8221;, IROP is considered a variable interest entity of which we are the primary beneficiary. As our significant asset is our investment in IROP, substantially all of our assets and liabilities represent the assets and liabilities of IROP.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c143727881" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>c. Use of Estimates</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting periods. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:center;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727882" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>d. Cash and Cash Equivalents</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Cash and cash equivalents include cash held in banks and highly liquid investments with original maturities of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less when purchased. Cash, including amounts restricted, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>at times exceed the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation deposit insurance limit of <em style="font: inherit;">$250</em>&#160;per institution. We mitigate credit risk by placing cash and cash equivalents with major financial institutions. To date, we have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> experienced any losses on cash and cash equivalents.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndCashEquivalentsPolicy" id="c143727883" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>e. Restricted Cash</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Restricted cash includes escrows of our funds held by lenders to fund certain expenditures, such as real estate taxes and insurance, or to be released at our discretion upon the occurrence of certain pre-specified events. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we had $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725833" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">19,926</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725835" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestrictedCash" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">24,058</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of restricted cash.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RealEstatePolicyTextBlock" id="c143727884" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>f. Investments in Real Estate</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Investments in real estate are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation. Costs, including internal costs, that both add value and appreciably extend the useful life of an asset are capitalized. Expenditures for repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Investments in real estate are classified as held for sale in the period in which certain criteria are met including when the sale of the asset is probable, necessary approvals are obtained, and actions required to complete the plan of sale indicate that it is unlikely that significant changes to the plan of sale will be made or the plan of sale will be withdrawn.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Allocation of Purchase Price of Acquired Assets</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">805</em> (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805&#8221;</em>), we evaluate our real estate acquisitions to determine if they should be accounted for as a business or as a group of assets. The evaluation includes an initial screen to determine if substantially all of the fair value of the gross assets acquired is concentrated in a single asset or group of similar assets. If the screen is met, the acquisition is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a business. The properties we have acquired met the screen test and are accounted for as asset acquisitions. Under asset acquisition accounting, the costs to acquire real estate, including transaction costs related to the acquisition, are accumulated and then allocated to the individual assets and liabilities acquired based upon their relative fair value. Transaction costs and fees incurred related to the financing of an acquisition are capitalized and amortized over the life of the related financing.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We estimate the fair value of acquired tangible assets (consisting of land, building and improvements), identified intangible assets (consisting of in-place leases), and assumed debt at the date of acquisition, based on the evaluation of information and estimates available at that date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The aggregate value of in-place leases is determined by evaluating various factors, including the terms of the leases that are in place and assumed lease-up periods. The value assigned to these intangible assets is amortized over the assumed lease up period, typically <em style="font: inherit;">nine</em> months. During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we acquired in-place leases with a value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725847" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinitelivedIntangibleAssetsAcquired1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">753</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725848" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinitelivedIntangibleAssetsAcquired1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,829</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, related to our acquisitions that are discussed further in Note <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;&#8220;Investments in Real Estate". During&#160;the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725852" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,159</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725853" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,853</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of amortization for intangible assets. For each of the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we wrote-off fully amortized <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725856">intangible assets</span> of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725857" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we expect to record additional amortization expense on current in-place intangible assets of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725859" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-12-31_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-LeasesAcquiredInPlaceMember_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,564</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the remainder of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Management evaluates the recoverability of our investments in real estate assets, including related identifiable intangible assets, in accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">360,</em> &#8220;Property, Plant and Equipment&#8221;. This accounting standard requires that long-lived assets be reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that recoverability of the assets is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> assured.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We review our long-lived assets on an ongoing basis and evaluate the recoverability of the carrying value when there is an indicator of impairment. An impairment charge is recognized when it is determined that the carrying value of the asset exceeds the fair value. The estimated cash flows and estimated fair value used in the impairment analysis are determined based on our plans for the respective assets, including the expected hold period, and our assessment of market and economic conditions. The estimates consider matters such as current and historical rental rates and collection levels, occupancies for the respective and/or comparable properties, and recent sales data for comparable properties. Changes in our plans or views of market and economic conditions <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in adjustments to estimated future cash flows, which could lead to recognition of impairment losses. These losses, as guided by the applicable accounting standards, could be significant.&#160;For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> we&#160;recorded <ix:nonFraction id="c143725865" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TangibleAssetImpairmentCharges" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725867">impairment charges</span>&#160;on account of real estate classified as held for sale and&#160;sold properties.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Depreciation Expense</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Depreciation expense for real estate assets is computed using a straight-line method based on a life of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2026-03-31_MortgageLoansOnRealEstateDescriptionTypeOfPropertyAxis-BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember" name="us-gaap:RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationLifeUsedForDepreciation1" id="c143725868" format="ixt-sec:duryear">40</ix:nonNumeric> years for buildings and improvements and <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725869">five</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725870">ten</span> years for furniture, fixtures, and equipment. For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725873" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SECScheduleIIIRealEstateAccumulatedDepreciationDepreciationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">61,952</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725874" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SECScheduleIIIRealEstateAccumulatedDepreciationDepreciationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">56,454</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of depreciation expense, respectively. During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we wrote-off fully depreciated fixed assets of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725877" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsHeldForUse" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">4,770</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725878" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsHeldForUse" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">7,792</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Casualty Related Costs</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Occasionally, we incur losses at our communities from wind storms, floods, fires and similar hazards.&#160;In these cases, we estimate the carrying value of the damaged property and record a casualty loss for the difference between the estimated carrying value and the insurance proceeds, if any. Any amount of insurance recovery in excess of the amount of the losses incurred is considered a gain contingency and is recorded in casualty losses (gains), net when the proceeds are received. During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725881" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnusualOrInfrequentItemNetOfInsuranceProceeds" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">77</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;($<ix:nonFraction id="c143725882" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnusualOrInfrequentItemNetOfInsuranceProceeds" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">115</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;of&#160;casualty&#160;losses (gains), net, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RealEstateHeldForDevelopmentAndSalePolicy" id="c143727885" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>g. Investments in Real Estate Under Development</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We capitalize direct and indirect project costs incurred during the development period such as construction, insurance, architectural, legal, interest costs, and real estate taxes. At such time as the development is considered substantially complete, the capitalization of certain indirect costs such as real estate taxes, interest costs, and all project-related costs in real estate under development are reclassified to investments in real estate. For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725885" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-InvestmentsInRealEstateUnderDevelopmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,557</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725886" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-InvestmentsInRealEstateUnderDevelopmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,559</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of capitalized interest expense on our investments in real estate under development.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the carrying value of our&#160;investments in real estate under development in Denver, Colorado and Austin, Texas&#160;totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725887" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:RealEstateInvestmentDevelopmentInProcessNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">127,840</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725888" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:RealEstateInvestmentDevelopmentInProcessNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">60,116</ix:nonFraction><span style="color:#ff0000">&#160;</span>respectively, net of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725889" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:RealEstateHeldForDevelopmentAndSalePlacedInServiceNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">120,773</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725890" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="irt:RealEstateHeldForDevelopmentAndSalePlacedInServiceNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">67,511</ix:nonFraction><span style="color:#ff0000">&#160;</span>placed in service, respectively, and was recorded as a separate line item in our condensed consolidated balance sheets.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentsPolicy" id="c143727886" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>h. Investments in Unconsolidated Real Estate Entities</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We have entered into joint ventures with unrelated <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties to acquire, develop, own, operate, and manage real estate assets. Our joint ventures are funded with a combination of debt and equity. We will consolidate entities that we control as well as any variable interest entity ("VIE") where we are the primary beneficiary. Under the VIE model, we consolidate an entity when we have the ability to direct the activities of the VIE and the obligations to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant to the VIE. Under the voting model, we consolidate an entity when we control the entity through ownership of a majority voting interest. We separately analyzed the initial accounting for each of our&#160;investments in unconsolidated real estate entities and concluded that each investment is a voting interest entity. Our equity interest varies for each of our&#160;investments in unconsolidated real estate entities between <ix:nonFraction id="c143725893" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-IndependenceRealtyTrustMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-InvestmentsInUnconsolidatedRealEstateEntitiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">66.6</ix:nonFraction>% and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143725894" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_OwnershipAxis-IndependenceRealtyTrustMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-InvestmentsInUnconsolidatedRealEstateEntitiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% but, in each case, we share control of the major decisions that most significantly impact the joint ventures with our partners. Since we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> control the joint venture through our ownership interest, they are accounted for under the equity method of accounting, and are included in investments in unconsolidated real estate entities on our&#160;condensed consolidated balance sheets. Under the equity method of accounting, the investments are carried at cost plus our share of net earnings or losses. For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we&#160;recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725898" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">519</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725899" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">954</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of capitalized interest expense on our investments in unconsolidated real estate entities in our condensed consolidated balance sheets.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727887" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>i. Revenue and Expenses</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Rental and Other Property Revenue</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We apply FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842,</em> &#8220;Leases&#8221; (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">842&#8221;</em>) with respect to our accounting for rental income. We primarily lease apartment units under operating leases generally with terms of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less. Rental payments are generally due monthly and rental revenues are recognized on an accrual basis when earned. We have elected to account for lease (i.e., fixed payments including base rent) and non-lease components (i.e., tenant reimbursements and certain other service fees) as a single combined operating lease component since (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) the timing and pattern of transfer of the lease and non-lease components is the same, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) the lease component is the predominant element, and (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) the combined single lease component would be classified as an operating lease.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We make ongoing estimates of the collectability of our base rents, tenant reimbursements, and other service fees included within rental and other property revenue. If collectability is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> probable, we adjust rental and other property income for the amount of uncollectible revenue.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727888" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>j. Derivative Instruments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use derivative financial instruments to hedge all or a portion of the interest rate risk associated with our borrowings. The principal objective of such arrangements is to minimize the risks and/or costs associated with our operating and financial structure, as well as to hedge specific anticipated transactions. While these instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>impact our periodic cash flows, they benefit us by minimizing the risks and/or costs previously described. The counterparties to these contractual arrangements are major financial institutions with which we, and our affiliates, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also have other financial relationships. In the event of nonperformance by the counterparties, we are potentially exposed to credit loss. However, because of the high credit ratings of the counterparties, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate that any of the counterparties will fail to meet their obligations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> &#8220;Derivatives and Hedging&#8221;, we measure each derivative instrument at fair value and record such amounts in our condensed consolidated balance sheets as either an asset or liability. For derivatives designated as cash flow hedges, the changes in the fair value of the effective portions of the derivative are reported in other comprehensive income and changes in the fair value of the ineffective portions of cash flow hedges, if any, are recognized in earnings. For derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges, the changes in fair value of the derivative instrument are recognized in earnings. Any derivatives that we designate in hedge relationships are done so at inception. At inception, we determine whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the derivative is highly effective in offsetting changes in the designated interest rate risk associated with the identified indebtedness using regression analysis. At each reporting period, we update our regression analysis and use the hypothetical derivative method to measure any ineffectiveness.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy" id="c143727889" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>k. Fair Value of Financial Instruments</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221;, fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Where available, fair value is based on observable market prices or parameters or derived from such prices or parameters. Where observable prices or inputs are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, valuation models are applied. These valuation techniques involve management estimation and judgment, the degree of which is dependent on the price transparency for the instruments or market and the instruments&#8217; complexity for disclosure purposes. Assets and liabilities recorded at fair value in our condensed consolidated balance sheets are categorized based upon the level of judgment associated with the inputs used to measure their value. Hierarchical levels, as defined in FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221; and directly related to the amount of subjectivity associated with the inputs to fair valuations of these assets and liabilities, are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em></b>: Valuations are based on unadjusted, quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities at the measurement date. The types of assets carried at Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> fair value generally are equity securities listed in active markets. As such, valuations of these investments do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> entail a significant degree of judgment.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em></b>: Valuations are based on quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets or quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active or for which all significant inputs are observable, either directly or indirectly.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em></b>: Inputs are unobservable for the asset or liability, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability. In certain cases, the inputs used to measure fair value <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fall into different levels of the fair value hierarchy. In such cases, the level in the fair value hierarchy within which the fair value measurement in its entirety falls has been determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety. Our assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment, and considers factors specific to the asset or liability.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">825,</em> &#8220;Financial Instruments&#8221; requires disclosure of the fair value of financial instruments for which it is practicable to estimate that value. Given that cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash are short term in nature with limited fair value volatility, the carrying amount is deemed to be a reasonable approximation of fair value and the fair value input is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> fair value measurement. The fair value input for derivatives is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> fair value measurement within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value of our unsecured revolver, term loans, and mortgage indebtedness is based on a discounted cash flows valuation technique. As this technique utilizes current credit spreads, which are generally unobservable, this is classified as a Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> fair value measurement within the fair value hierarchy. We determine appropriate credit spreads based on the type of debt and its maturity. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transfers between levels in the fair value hierarchy for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. The following table summarizes the carrying amount and the fair value of our financial instruments as of the periods indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DeferredChargesPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727890" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>l. Deferred Financing Costs</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Costs incurred in connection with debt financing are deferred and classified within indebtedness and charged to interest expense over the terms of the related debt agreements, under the effective interest method.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727891" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>m. Office Leases</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In accordance with FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842,</em> &#8220;Leases&#8221;, lessees are required to recognize a right-of-use asset and a lease liability on the balance sheet at the lease commencement date for all leases, except those leases with terms of less than a year. We lease corporate office space under leases with terms of up to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2026-03-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c143725928" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years and that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include extension options, but that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include any residual value guarantees or restrictive covenants. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we had&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725930" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,617</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725931" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,771</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of operating lease right-of-use assets and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725932" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,915</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143725933" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,082</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of operating lease liabilities related to our corporate office leases. The operating lease right-of-use assets are presented within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725934"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725935">other assets</span></span> and the operating lease liabilities are presented within <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725936"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143725937">other liabilities</span></span> in our condensed consolidated balance sheets. During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725940" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">196</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143725941" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">120</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;respectively, of total operating lease expense which is recorded within property management expense and general and administrative expenses in our condensed consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727892" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 14pt;text-indent:9pt;"><b><i>n. Income Taxes</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We have elected to be taxed as a REIT. Accordingly, we recorded <ix:nonFraction id="c143725942" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> income tax expense for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">To qualify as a REIT, we must meet certain organizational and operational requirements, including a requirement to distribute at least <em style="font: inherit;">90%</em> of our ordinary taxable income to stockholders. As a REIT, we generally are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to federal income tax on taxable income that we distribute to our stockholders. If we fail to qualify as a REIT in any taxable year, we will be subject to federal income taxes on our taxable income at regular corporate rates and will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be permitted to qualify for treatment as a REIT for federal income tax purposes for <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> years following the year during which qualification is lost unless the Internal Revenue Service grants us relief under certain statutory provisions. Such an event could materially adversely affect our net income and net cash available for distribution to stockholders; however, we believe that we are organized and operate in such a manner as to qualify and maintain treatment as a REIT and intend to operate in such a manner so that we will remain qualified as a REIT for federal income tax purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:23pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c143727893" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:23pt;"><b><i>o. Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Below is a brief description of recent accounting pronouncements that could have a material effect on our condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;)&#160;issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12,</em> <i>Codification Improvements</i>, as part of its ongoing project to clarify, correct and improve various topics within the Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;). The amendments cover <em style="font: inherit;">33</em> specific issues, <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> of which are particularly relevant to REITs, (i) clarifications on the calculation of diluted earnings per share when a loss from continuing operations exists (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">260</em>), and (ii) the exclusion of certain lease receivables from enhanced credit loss disclosures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">310</em>). The standard is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those years. Early adoption is permitted on an issue-by-issue basis. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12</em> on its consolidated financial position, results of operations and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>): Hedge Accounting Improvements</i>. The update is designed to better align hedge accounting with an entity's risk management activities by making targeted improvements to the hedge accounting model. Key amendments include, Similar Risk Assessment, which replaces the &#8220;shared risk exposure&#8221; requirement for grouping forecasted transactions in a cash flow hedge with a &#8220;similar risk exposure&#8221; requirement, permitting broader aggregation of hedged risks, Choose-Your-Rate Debt which introduces a model for hedging interest payments on variable-rate borrowings where the borrower can change reference rates without automatically triggering hedge de-designation, and Net Written Options which clarifies that certain instruments, such as, interest rate swaps with floors, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>qualify as hedging instruments without being subject to the net written option test, provided. The standard is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within those years. Early adoption is permitted. The guidance is generally required to be applied on a prospective basis. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> on its consolidated financial position, results of operations and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>, which requires disclosure of information about specific cost and expense categories in the notes to the financial statements. This ASU is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods&#160;beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and for interim reporting periods commencing in <em style="font: inherit;">2028</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied either prospectively or retrospectively. The Company is currently evaluating the effect that the ASU will have on its consolidated financial position, results of operations and disclosures.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Unsecured Revolver and Term Loans&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February, 11, 2026, </em>IROP entered into the Sixth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the &#8220;Sixth Restated Credit Agreement&#8221;) by and among IROP, as borrower, IRT as parent guarantor, KeyBank National Association, as administrative agent, and the other agents and lender parties thereto, which amended and restated in its entirety the Fifth Amended and Restated Credit agreement dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2025 (</em>the &#8220;Fifth Restated Credit Agreement&#8221;). The Fifth Restated Credit Agreement provided for a $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726187" contextRef="i_2025-01-08_CreditFacilityAxis-UnsecuredRevolverMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">750,000</ix:nonFraction> unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Unsecured Revolver&#8221;) with a <em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2029 </em>scheduled maturity date and <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> unsecured term loans, specifically: (i) a $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726189" contextRef="i_2025-01-08_CreditFacilityAxis-TermLoanFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">200,000</ix:nonFraction> term loan with a <em style="font: inherit;"> May 18, 2026 </em>maturity date (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2026</em> Term Loan&#8221;) and (ii) a $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726191" contextRef="i_2025-01-08_CreditFacilityAxis-TermLoanFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-A2028TermLoanMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">400,000</ix:nonFraction> term loan with a <em style="font: inherit;"> January 28, 2028 </em>maturity date (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2028</em> Term Loan&#8221;). The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement provides for a new $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726193" contextRef="i_2026-02-11_CreditFacilityAxis-TermLoanFacilityMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-SixthRestatedCreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">350.0</ix:nonFraction> million unsecured term loan with a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 11, 2030, </em>subject to a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year extension option (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2030</em> Term Loan&#8221;). A portion of the proceeds from the <em style="font: inherit;">2030</em> Term Loan were used to pay off outstanding borrowings under the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Term Loan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> holders of IROP units exchanged&#160;units for&#160;shares of our common stock. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726446" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:LimitedPartnersCapitalAccountUnitsOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,941,643</ix:nonFraction> IROP units held by unaffiliated <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties remain outstanding.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 9, 2026</em>, our board of directors declared a dividend of $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726448" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DividendsAxis-O2026Q1DividendsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="irt:UnitDividendsPerShareDeclared" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.17</ix:nonFraction>&#160;per IROP unit, which was paid on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 17, 2026</em> to IROP unit holders of record as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2026</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">8:</em> Equity Compensation Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;"><i>Long Term Incentive Plan</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 18, 2022, </em>our stockholders approved our&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Long Term Incentive Plan (the &#8220;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan&#8221;).&#160;The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan provides for grants of equity and equity-based awards to our employees, officers, directors, consultants and other service providers, and such awards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>take the form of restricted or unrestricted shares of common stock, non-qualified stock options, incentive stock options, restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;), dividend equivalents and other equity and cash-based awards. A maximum of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726458" contextRef="i_2022-05-18_PlanNameAxis-LongTermIncentivePlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of our common stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued under the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan (plus up to an additional&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726460" contextRef="d_2022-05-18_2022-05-18_PlanNameAxis-LongTermIncentivePlanMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Share" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardNumberOfAdditionalSharesPotentiallyRecycledIntoTheStockPlan" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">702,300</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of our common stock remain available from our prior incentive plan, to the extent that shares subject to outstanding awards under a&#160;prior plan are recycled into the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Plan), subject to customary adjustment for stock splits, reverse stock splits and similar corporate events or transactions affecting shares of our common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The restricted shares and RSUs granted under the Incentive Plan generally vest or vested over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726462">two</span>-to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726463">four</span>-year period. In addition, we have granted unrestricted shares to our non-employee directors. These awards generally vest or vested immediately. A summary of restricted and unrestricted common share awards and RSU activity is presented below.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 3, 2026, </em>our compensation committee awarded&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726467" contextRef="d_2026-02-03_2026-02-03_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceShareUnitsPsusMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">194,574</ix:nonFraction>&#160;performance share units (&#8220;PSUs&#8221;) (measured at target) to our executive officers. The number of PSUs earned will be based on attainment of certain performance criteria over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726468">three</span>-year period, with the actual number of shares issuable ranging between&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726469" contextRef="i_2026-02-03_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceShareUnitsPsusMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationPercentOfIssuableShares" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>% and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726470" contextRef="i_2026-02-03_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceShareUnitsPsusMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="irt:SharebasedCompensationPercentOfIssuableShares" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">150</ix:nonFraction>% of the target number of PSUs granted. Half of any PSUs earned will vest, and shares will be issued in respect thereof, immediately following the end of the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726471">three</span>-year performance period; the remaining half of any PSUs earned will vest, and shares will be issued in respect thereof, after an additional <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726472">one</span>-year period of service.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, a portion of the RSUs and PSUs granted were issued to employees who are retirement eligible. The fact that the grantees are retirement eligible resulted in immediate recognition of the associated stock-based compensation expense totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c143726475" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,437</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143726476" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,826</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3166670" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE <em style="font: inherit;">10:</em> Segment Reporting</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Each of our multifamily properties is considered an operating segment that earns revenues through the leasing of apartment homes and incurs associated expenses.&#160;We aggregate our multifamily properties on a same-store and non same-store basis, and as a result, have identified <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143726526">two</span> reportable segments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 45pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Same-Store includes properties that were owned and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a development property as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025, </em>and that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been sold or identified as held for sale.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 45pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Non Same-Store includes properties that did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the definition of a same-store property as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025.</em></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">GAAP guidance requires that segment disclosures present the measures used by the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) to decide how to allocate resources and for purposes of assessing segment performance.&#160;The CODM uses net operating income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;) as the primary financial measure to evaluate operating results of our multifamily properties, including analyses compared to prior periods and budgeted operating results. NOI is defined as total property revenues less total property operating expenses, excluding interest expenses, depreciation and amortization, casualty related costs and gains, property management expenses, general and administrative expense and net gains on sale of assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Segment assets consist of real estate held for investment, real estate held for sale and investments in real estate under development. Non-segment assets consist of assets in the Company&#8217;s other non-reportable segments and corporate non-segment assets, which are comprised of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, investments in unconsolidated real estate entities, other assets, derivative assets and intangible assets. Reportable segment asset information is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provided to the CODM as the CODM does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> use segment asset information to evaluate the business and allocate resources.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The following table details NOI for our&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c143726532" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">two</ix:nonFraction>&#160;reportable segments for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;and reconciles&#160;NOI to Net&#160;(loss) income on the condensed consolidated statements of operations. The segments are classified as same-store or non same-store based on the individual property&#8217;s status as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p>
