   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>NOTE</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">11:</em> Other Disclosures&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We are subject to various legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of our business operations. Matters which arise out of allegations of bodily injury, property damage,&#160;employment practices and professional liability are generally covered by insurance. While the resolution of these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, we currently believe the final outcome of such matters will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Starting around <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022, </em>putative class action representatives began filing complaints in various United States District Courts across the country naming as defendants RealPage, Inc. (&#8220;RealPage&#8221;), a seller of revenue management products, and approximately <em style="font: inherit;">50</em> defendants who own and/or manage multifamily residential rental housing, alleging that the defendants conspired to fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize rent prices in violation of Section <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the Sherman Act. Some of the complaints, including <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> filed on <em style="font: inherit;"> November 14, 2022, </em>in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, named us as <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the defendants, and others did <em style="font: inherit;">not.</em> The actions were consolidated for pretrial proceedings in the Middle District of Tennessee. Discovery is ongoing. It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> possible for the Company to estimate the amount of loss, if any, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be associated with an adverse decision in this matter. We deny all allegations of wrongdoing and intend to defend against these claims vigorously.&#160;See Part II, Item <em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> <i>Legal Proceedings</i>, for additional information regarding our legal proceedings.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Other Matters</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">To the extent that a natural disaster or similar event occurs with more than a remote risk of having a material impact on the consolidated financial statements, we will disclose the estimated range of possible outcomes, and, if an outcome is probable, accrue an appropriate liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Loss Contingencies</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We record an accrual for loss contingencies when a loss is probable and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated. Management reviews these accruals quarterly and makes revisions based on changes in facts and circumstances. When a loss contingency is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> both probable and reasonably estimable, management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrue the loss. However, if the loss (or an additional loss in excess of an earlier accrual) is at least a reasonable possibility and material, then management discloses a reasonable estimate of the possible loss, or range of loss, if such reasonable estimate can be made. If we cannot make a reasonable estimate of the possible loss, or range of loss, then a statement to that effect is disclosed.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Our Company</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We are a self-administered and self-managed Maryland corporation that has elected to be taxed as a real estate investment trust (&#8220;REIT&#8221;). We are primarily engaged in the ownership, operation, management, improvement, and acquisition of multifamily apartment communities in non-gateway markets. As of March 31, 2026, we owned and operated 115&#160;multifamily apartment properties (including one owned through a consolidated joint venture) that contain an aggregate of&#160;33,602 units. Our properties are located in Alabama, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee and Texas. In addition, as of March 31, 2026, we owned two newly developed properties, including one&#160;in Denver, Colorado, that contains&#160;296&#160;units and one&#160;in Austin, Texas that&#160;contains&#160;378 units. As of March 31, 2026, we also owned interests in three&#160;unconsolidated joint ventures, one of which&#160;owns and operates a multifamily apartment community&#160;that contains&#160;275&#160;units and two of which that are&#160;developing multifamily apartment communities&#160;that will contain, upon completion, an aggregate of&#160;642&#160;units. We do not have any foreign operations and our business is not seasonal.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Our Business Objective and Investment Strategies </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our primary business objective is to maximize stockholder value through diligent portfolio management, strong operational performance, and a consistent return of capital through distributions and capital appreciation. Our investment strategy is focused on the following:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">

     <td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#8226;</p> </td>
     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">gaining scale within key amenity rich submarkets of non-gateway cities that offer good school districts, high-quality retail and major employment centers and are unlikely to experience substantial new apartment construction in the foreseeable future;</p> </td>
    </tr>

     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">increasing cash flows at our existing apartment properties through prudent property management and strategic renovation projects; and</p> </td>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Current Developments</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Acquisitions </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On January 15, 2026, we acquired The Retreat at Canal in&#160;Columbus, Ohio, a 140-unit community for $29.5 million. The acquisition increased our exposure in Columbus, Ohio from 2,510 units to 2,650 units.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Investments in Unconsolidated Real Estate Entities</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">To create another avenue for accretive capital allocation and to increase our options for capital investment, we have partnered with, and may in the future partner with, developers through preferred equity investments and joint venture relationships focused on new multifamily development.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On January 20, 2026, we acquired our joint venture partner's 10% membership interest&#160;and assumed full operational control and 100% equity ownership of the Tisdale at Lakeline Station property underlying this joint venture. The property is a newly constructed 378-unit community in Austin, Texas and was consolidated into our financial results effective January 20, 2026. The property will be classified as a development property until reaching 90% occupancy.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, we had investments in unconsolidated real estate entities of $66.6&#160;million and $98.3&#160;million, respectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Investments in Real Estate Under Development</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">As of March 31, 2026, we had two investments in real estate under development&#160;of $127.8  million, which&#160;contain an aggregate of 674 units&#160;and are currently in lease-up.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Value Add Initiative</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Strategically renovating communities where there is the potential for outsized rent growth (our "Value Add Initiative") provides us with the opportunity to improve long-term growth through targeted unit and/or common area investments. We completed renovations on 426&#160;units during the three months ended March 31, 2026. From inception of our Value Add Initiative&#160;in January 2018 through March 31, 2026, we completed renovations on&#160;11,871 of the&#160;18,788 units currently in our Value Add Initiative, achieving a return on investment of&#160;16.1% (and approximately&#160;18.1% on the interior portion of such renovation costs). We compute return on investment&#160;by using the rent premium per unit per month, multiplied by 12, divided by the applicable renovation costs per unit and we compute the rent premium as the difference between the rental rate on the renovated unit (excluding the impact of concessions) and the market rent for a comparable unrenovated unit as of the date presented, as determined by management consistent with its customary rent-setting and evaluation procedures.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Capital Markets</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i><b>Unsecured Revolver and Term Loans</b></i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On February 11, 2026, Independence Realty Operating Partnership, LP (&#8220;IROP&#8221;) entered into the Sixth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the &#8220;Sixth Restated Credit Agreement&#8221;) by and among IROP, as borrower, Independence Realty Trust, Inc., as parent guarantor, KeyBank National Association, as administrative agent, and the other agents and lender parties thereto, which amended and restated in its entirety the Fifth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated as of January 8, 2025 (the &#8220;Fifth Restated Credit Agreement&#8221;). The Fifth Restated Credit Agreement provided for a $750.0 million unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Unsecured Revolver&#8221;) with a January 8, 2029 scheduled maturity date and two unsecured term loans, specifically: (i) a $200.0 million term loan with a May 18, 2026 maturity date (the &#8220;2026 Term Loan&#8221;) and (ii) a $400.0 million term loan with a January 28, 2028 maturity date (the &#8220;2028 Term Loan&#8221;). The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement provides for a new $350.0 million unsecured term loan with a maturity date of February 11, 2030, subject to a one year extension option (the &#8220;2030 Term Loan&#8221;). A portion of the proceeds from the 2030 Term Loan were used to pay off outstanding borrowings under the 2026 Term Loan.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Sixth Restated Credit Agreement also increases the aggregate amount of borrowings under the credit agreement to $1.5 billion and permits IROP to request the capacity be further&#160;increased to $2.0 billion subject to certain terms and conditions, including receipt of commitments from one or more lenders, whether or not currently parties to the Sixth Restated Credit Agreement, to provide such increased amounts, which increase may be allocated, at IROP&#8217;s option, to the Unsecured Revolver and/or to one or more of the Term Loans, in accordance with the Sixth Restated Credit Agreement.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>ATM Program</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On July 28, 2023, we entered into an equity distribution agreement pursuant to which we may from time to time offer and sell shares of our common stock under our shelf registration statement having an aggregate offering price of up to $450.0 million (the &#8220;ATM Program&#8221;) in negotiated transactions or transactions that are deemed to be &#8220;at the market&#8221; offerings as defined in Rule 415 under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;). Under the ATM Program, we may also enter into one or more forward sale transactions for the sale of shares of our common stock on a forward basis. There were no forward sale transactions and no shares of our common stock were sold under the ATM Program during the three months ended March 31, 2026.&#160;As of March 31, 2026, approximately $342.4 million&#160;remained available for issuance under the&#160;ATM Program.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Stock Repurchase Program</i></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 8pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On May 18, 2022, our board of directors authorized a common stock repurchase program (the "Stock Repurchase Program") covering up to $250.0 million&#160;in shares of our common stock. Under the Stock Repurchase Program, we, in our discretion, may purchase our shares from time to time in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions. The amount and timing of the purchases will depend on a number of factors, including the price and availability of our shares, trading volumes and general market conditions. The Stock Repurchase Program has no time limit and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, we&#160;repurchased and retired 1.8 million&#160;shares of common stock&#160;under our&#160;Stock Repurchase Program at a weighted average price of $16.24 per share at a total cost of $29.9 million. As of March 31, 2026, $190.1 million&#160;in shares of our common stock remained&#160;authorized for repurchase under our&#160;Stock Repurchase Program.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Revenue</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Rental and other property revenue</i>. Revenue from rental and other property revenue of the consolidated portfolio increased&#160;$4.3&#160;million to&#160;$165.2 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from $160.9&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The increase was&#160;attributable to a $2.2&#160;million increase in non same-store rental and other property revenue primarily driven by the acquisition of three&#160;properties in 2025 earning a full quarter of rental and other property revenue in 2026 and a&#160;$2.1 million increase in&#160;same-store rental and other property revenue driven by higher other income, lower bad debt and higher average monthly rent compared to the prior year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Expenses </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Property operating expenses<span style="color:#000000">.&#160;</span></i><span style="color:#000000">Property operating expenses&#160;increased</span><span style="color:#000000">&#160;$2.9</span><span style="color:#000000">&#160;million to&#160;$62.1</span><span style="color:#000000">&#160;million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="color:#000000"> from&#160;$59.3</span><span style="color:#000000">&#160;million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2025<span style="color:#000000">. The increase was primarily driven by a&#160;$1.7&#160;million increase in non same-store operating expenses due&#160;to the acquisition of&#160;three properties in 2025 incurring a full quarter of operating expenses in 2026. In addition, the $1.1 million increase in same-store operating expenses was due to higher payroll costs, utilities and&#160;contract services, partially offset by lower insurance expenses.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="color:#000000"><i>Property management expenses.</i> Property management expenses increased&#160;$0.4 million to $8.2&#160;million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="color:#000000"> from $7.8&#160;million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2025<span style="color:#000000">.<i>&#160;</i>The increase was primarily driven by the timing of property management expenses in 2025 compared to 2026 and due&#160;to an increase in new hire training costs during the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="color:#000000">,&#160;compared to the same prior year period.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Depreciation<span style="color:#000000;"> and amortization expense.</span></i><span style="color:#000000;"> <span style="font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,serif;">Depreciation and amortization expense&#160;</span></span><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,serif;">increased<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span>$5.9<span style="color:#000000;"> million to&#160;</span>$64.6<span style="color:#000000;"> million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2026<span style="color:#000000;"> from&#160;</span>$58.7<span style="color:#000000;"> million for the three months ended </span>March 31, 2025<span style="color:#000000;">. The increase was primarily due to depreciation expenses driven by capital expenditures related to our Value Add Initiative&#160;and higher intangible asset amortization expenses from our recent property acquisitions in 2025 and 2026 compared to the same prior year period.</span></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Interest expense</i>. Interest expense increased&#160;$1.4 million to&#160;$20.7 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from&#160;$19.3 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The increase during the three months ended March 31, 2026, was primarily driven by the higher average debt balance associated with our acquisitions and a decrease in capitalized interest associated with our real estate under development.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><i>&#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160;Gain on sale of real estate assets, net. </i>During<i>&#160;</i>the<i>&#160;</i>three months ended March 31, 2025, we sold one multi-family property resulting in a gain on sale of $1.5 million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;"><i>Loss from investments in unconsolidated real estate entities</i>. Loss from investments in unconsolidated real estate entities increased $0.4&#160;million to $1.0 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026 from $0.6&#160;million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. The increase&#160;in loss from investments in unconsolidated real estate entities is primarily driven by an&#160;increase in depreciation expense from&#160;our unconsolidated real estate entities&#160;during the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to&#160;the three months ended March 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160; &#160; &#160;&#160;<b>Non-GAAP Financial Measures </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Funds from Operations (FFO) and Core Funds from Operations (CFFO)</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We believe that FFO and Core FFO (&#8220;CFFO&#8221;), each of which is a non-GAAP financial measure, are additional appropriate measures of the operating performance of a REIT and us in particular. We compute FFO in accordance with the standards established by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts (&#8220;NAREIT&#8221;), as net income or loss allocated to common shares (computed in accordance with GAAP), excluding real estate-related depreciation and amortization expense, gains or losses on sales of real estate and the cumulative effect of changes in accounting principles. While our calculation of FFO is in accordance with NAREIT&#8217;s definition, it may differ from the methodology for calculating FFO utilized by other REITs and, accordingly, may not be comparable to FFO computations of such other REITs.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">CFFO is a computation made by analysts and investors to measure a real estate company&#8217;s operating performance by removing the effect of items that do not reflect ongoing property operations, including depreciation and amortization of other items not included in FFO, and other non-cash or non-operating gains or losses related to items such as casualty (gains) losses, loan premium accretion and discount amortization and debt extinguishment costs&#160;from the determination of FFO.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Our calculation of CFFO may differ from the methodology used for calculating CFFO by other REITs and, accordingly, our CFFO may not be comparable to CFFO reported by other REITs. Our management utilizes FFO and CFFO as measures of our operating performance, and believe they are also useful to investors, because they facilitate an understanding of our operating performance after adjustment for certain non-cash or non-recurring items that are required by GAAP to be expensed but may not necessarily be indicative of current operating performance and our operating performance between periods. Furthermore, although FFO, CFFO and other supplemental performance measures are defined in various ways throughout the REIT industry, we believe that FFO and CFFO may provide us and our investors with an additional useful measure to compare our financial performance to certain other REITs. Neither FFO nor CFFO is equivalent to net income or cash generated from operating activities determined in accordance with GAAP. Furthermore, FFO and CFFO do not represent amounts available for management&#8217;s discretionary use because of needed capital replacement or expansion, debt service obligations or other commitments or uncertainties. Accordingly, FFO and CFFO do not measure whether cash flow is sufficient to fund all of our cash needs, including principal amortization and capital improvements. Neither FFO nor CFFO should be considered as an alternative to net income or any other GAAP measurement as an indicator of our operating performance or as an alternative to cash flow from operating, investing, and financing activities as a measure of our liquidity.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Same-Store Portfolio Net Operating Income </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We believe that Net Operating Income (&#8220;NOI&#8221;), a non-GAAP financial measure, is a useful supplemental measure of our operating performance. We define NOI as total property revenues less total property operating expenses, excluding interest expenses, depreciation and amortization, casualty related costs and gains, property management expenses, general and administrative expense and&#160;net gains on sale of assets. Other REITs may use different methodologies for calculating NOI, and accordingly, our NOI may not be comparable to other REITs. We believe that this measure provides an operating perspective not immediately apparent from GAAP operating income or net income insofar as the measure reflects only operating income and expense at the property level. We use NOI to evaluate our performance on a same-store and non same-store basis because NOI measures the core operations of property performance by excluding corporate level expenses, financing expenses, and other items not related to property operating performance and captures trends in rental housing and property operating expenses. However, NOI should only be used as an alternative measure of our financial performance.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Same-Store Properties and Same-Store Portfolio</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We review our same-store portfolio at the beginning of each calendar year. Properties are added into the same-store portfolio if they were owned and not a development property at the beginning of the previous year. Properties that are held for sale or have been sold are excluded from the same-store portfolio.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Non Same-Store Properties and Non Same-Store Portfolio</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Properties that did not meet the definition of a same-store property as of the beginning of the previous year are added into the non same-store portfolio.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Average Effective Monthly Rent per Unit</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Average effective rent per unit represents the average of net rent amounts, after concessions amortized over the life of the lease, divided by the average occupancy (in units) for the period presented. We believe average effective rent is a helpful measurement in evaluating average pricing. This metric, when presented, reflects the average effective rent per month.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Average Occupancy</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Average occupancy represents the average occupied units for the reporting period divided by the average of total units available for rent for the reporting period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Development Property</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">A development property is a property that is either currently under development or is in lease-up prior to reaching overall occupancy of 90%.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

We believe our available cash balances, financing arrangements and cash flows from operations will be sufficient to fund our liquidity requirements with respect to our existing portfolio for the next twelve months and the foreseeable future.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="legal" title="legal" href="#"></a>Item 1.</b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Legal Proceedings.</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We are subject to various legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of our business operations. Matters which arise out of allegations of bodily injury, property damage,&#160;employment practices and professional liability are generally covered by insurance. While the resolution of these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, we currently believe the final outcome of such matters will not have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">On&#160;July 2, 2025, the Attorney General of Kentucky filed a complaint against RealPage and nine other defendants who own and/or manage multifamily residential rental housing, including IRT, on behalf of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, also alleging that the defendants conspired to fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize rent prices in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act. On September 15, 2025, IRT and other defendants in the complaint filed motions to dismiss the case. On February 2, 2026, the court denied the motions to dismiss. This proceeding is in the early stages, and it is not possible for IRT&#160;to predict the outcome nor is it possible to estimate the amount of loss, if any, which may be associated with an adverse decision in this matter. We deny all allegations of wrongdoing in connection with the complaint and intend to defend against these claims vigorously.&#160;We are engaged in certain other legal proceedings, as disclosed&#160;in&#160;Note 11,&#160;&#8220;Other Disclosures&#8211;Litigation&#8221;<i>,</i>&#160;which disclosure is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
